"" "D4- My official Christmas ‘card’ to my beloved audience who observe it either as part of their faith, or philosophical stance, or tradition, or art expression, or cultural exercise published in a newspaper https://lnkd.in/gbd_fhMD "Christmas reflection on climate crisis Christmas, as a moment of renewal, invites alignment between our inner lives and the outer world humanity seeks to protect."" "" "Christmas, at its core, is a profound tradition that transcends commercialization, reminding us of relationships—between self, others, and the environment and The Christ. These relationships shape how we address challenges like the climate crisis." "" "In today’s polarized discussions on climate change, divided into believers and skeptics, the relational framework of Christmas offers a unique perspective. It calls for stewardship and shared responsibility, urging us to protect the Earth not as a resource but as a sacred trust for future generations." "" "Nevertheless, Christmas is often misunderstood or dismissed. Some view it as a commercialized holiday, stripped of meaning by consumerism. Others critique it as a pagan ritual, borrowed and repurposed by later traditions. From a religious perspective, some question its theological authenticity. Carl Sagan, in The Demon-Haunted World, warned of a future where critical thinking and scientific understanding might erode. He envisioned a society where misinformation, superstition, and fleeting opinions overshadow reason and knowledge. His words feel especially relevant today as digital platforms dominate how information is consumed and shape public perceptions." "" "This is evident in how people increasingly rely on their chosen channels of information—channels that, through algorithmic design, reinforce biases and flood minds with unchecked narratives. For example, some genuinely believed that a vice president's appointment could be annulled due to alleged procedural defects, a claim driven by speculative commentary. Ironically, this is the same vice president who gained infamy for confusing “pholiat acid” with “acid sulphate” when discussing baby milk and openly stated that he preferred comics over reading (difficult) books. Yet, despite this background, public discourse surrounding his appointment was shaped more by unchecked claims than factual evidence. Ultimately, time clarified the situation as the oath of office was sworn." "" "Another example highlights the dangers of relying on biased narratives: the significant loss of a candidate from a party symbolized by the raging bull. Many, relying on overly partisan news streams, expected a dominant victory but were blindsided when the candidate failed to even secure a significant percentage, despite the party’s dominant position in parliament. " "" "In an article I wrote for The Jakarta Post (https://lnkd.in/dagDcgjZ and https://lnkd.in/g8FQ3ve2), I explored a related idea through the philosophical lens of doxa (opinion) and episteme (grounded knowledge). While digital platforms often amplify doxa—unverified beliefs or fleeting trends—traditional journalism serves as a vital defender of episteme. Newspapers, with their rigorous editorial processes and commitment to verified information, create a space for reflective engagement, helping readers critically assess what is presented as fact versus mere opinion." "" "I discussed thinkers like Michel Foucault whose concept is that episteme as  the foundational framework of knowledge in any era, shaping societal perceptions. Similarly, Pierre Bourdieu’s understanding of doxa as ingrained societal beliefs further illustrated the challenge of navigating between popular consensus and verified truths in the digital age." "" "In today’s fast-paced world, the challenge is not just consuming information but discerning credible knowledge (episteme) from popular consensus (doxa). How do we ensure that episteme prevails over doxa in shaping public discourse?" "" "Traditional newspapers play a crucial role in meeting this challenge. By fostering deeper understanding and reflective consumption, they anchor society in truth amidst the noise of modern media. This distinction is more important than ever as we face an age increasingly shaped by fleeting content and emotional reactions.

2024-10-07 The embryo of my autoethnography began with a simple yet profound case note—"Process Obser...
The embryo of my autoethnography began with a simple yet profound case note—"Process Observation" by John J. Gabarro and Anne Harlan. This work taught me the value of observing interactions: who speaks, who remains silent, and how influence flows within groups. It laid the foundation for my fascination with the unspoken dynamics of human behavior, a curiosity that has shaped my journey ever since. It all started in 2000, during my OB MBA class with Prof. Derry Habir, a mentor whose rich stories of Indonesia’s diplomatic history taught me that every narrative holds deeper cultural meanings. From learning the disciplined analysis of case studies to uncovering the subtleties of social interactions through frameworks like Edgar Schein’s organizational culture and James P. Spradley’s Participant Observation, I discovered that observation is more than just a skill—it’s a way of seeing the world." "" "Autoethnography became my way of weaving together these experiences—connecting the personal and the professional, the intimate and the academic. Inspired by the works of Tony E. Adams, Carolyn Ellis, Arthur P. Bochner, and Heewon Chang et al (the giants of autoethnography), I embraced this method as a means to explore how our own stories can illuminate larger societal themes. Their insights into reflexivity, narrative, and the power of self-reflection have guided my approach. " "" "For me, autoethnography is like listening to Clair de Lune by Debussy—a way of shifting perspective to see the silvery, hidden nuances in everyday life. It’s a practice of asking “so what?”—of understanding why our stories matter and what they reveal about the world around us.

However, this does not excuse a lack of ignorance or idiocracy or perhaps on the contrary his super high IQ, because the Orde Baru period is widely covered in the Indonesian school curriculum, and the information is easily accessible through books, media, and the internet. " "" "An audience member remarked, “It reveals not just ignorance, but a more concerning lack of sense-making—a crucial leadership trait.”" "" "I sip my coffee, reflecting on this, and think: hmm, yes. A leader must possess the ability to understand and interpret history, drawing valuable lessons from it to inform present and future decisions. " "" "George Santayana, in The Life of Reason (1905) *), famously said: 🎠 "Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it." 🎠 " "" "Santayana's words emphasize the crucial role that historical awareness plays in shaping a society’s future. A leader who lacks this understanding runs the risk of making short-sighted, reactionary decisions, ultimately leading the nation back to mistakes that could have been avoided if they had learned from history." "" "For young people and voters of all ages, it’s crucial to reflect on the importance of choosing leaders who demonstrate a capacity for sense-making—the ability to connect the dots between historical events and current challenges. A leader who admits to being uninformed about key periods in their nation’s history may also lack the ability to apply critical lessons when faced with present-day issues." "" "Leadership is not just about charisma or popularity—it demands visioning, relating, executing, sense-making, and moral ethics. A leader must, over time, develop their talents by working and accumulating knowledge, where wisdom is a crucial outcome." "" "So, for voters, the question becomes: "Can we trust a leader who admits ignorance of the past, despite having access to vast amounts of information, to guide us forward? Or are we risking a return to the same mistakes that have held us back before?"" "" "*) Santayana, G. (1905). The life of reason: The phases of human progress. Scribner’s.

At times, I’ve felt completely alone, pushing forward without the resources that could make a difference." "" "But recently, something happened that reminded me why I keep going. In a crucial moment before our demo day, two of my senior team members, Nicholas Sidharta and Richard Mote, stepped up—without being asked—to organize in buying him a new pair of shoes and sandals. It wasn’t about the shoes; it was about community. Even when we don’t have much, we give. " "" "This is the "home" we’ve built—a place where acts of kindness come naturally, where faith and commitment drive us to keep going. 2024-08-18 Pleased to share that my latest article, "Engineers and Indonesia’s Path to Renewable Solu...
Pleased to share that my latest article, "Engineers and Indonesia’s Path to Renewable Solutions," has been published today August 19, 2024 in The Jakarta Post. This publication is particularly special, as it was originally intended for Indonesia's Independence Day on August 17, 2024, but due to the public holiday, it has only been published today, August 19, 2024 and it was submitted while I was in Boston. " "" "Our future engineers need more than just technical expertise—they need the right mindset and values to navigate the challenges ahead. By recognizing their potential and supporting their growth, we can ensure they are well-prepared to lead Indonesia into 2045 and beyond. It's up to all of us to foster an environment where these bright minds can thrive and contribute meaningfully to a sustainable future." "" "In my previous articles, I explored Indonesia’s nuclear energy landscape through three critical lenses: political, cultural, and structural. These perspectives offered deep insights into the multifaceted challenges and opportunities confronting our nuclear engineering and engineering physics communities." "" "Here’s a recap of the journey:" "- Political Lens: Highlighted the importance of diplomatic strategies and international alliances in advancing energy policies. https://lnkd.in/gcjEKR77" "- Cultural Lens: Emphasized the critical role of leadership and the cultural dynamics in executing large-scale energy projects.https://https://lnkd.in/gFHDdDaS " "- Structural Lens: Explored how innovations like SMRs and microreactors can serve Indonesia’s specific needs, using our existing nuclear expertise. https://lnkd.in/gJMQCZaJ" "" "Today's article brings these insights together to focus on the future of our energy engineers. The opportunities in SMRs, renewable energy, and Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) are there—but realizing them requires collaboration among all stakeholders. This isn't just about adjusting structures; it's about seeing our students and professionals not as numbers, but as lifelong learners, contributors to humanity, and torchbearers of the Golden Indonesia 2045 vision." "" "Key takeaways from my latest article:" "- The transition to renewables and climate change solutions offers a bright future for nuclear and physics engineers." "- Failing to effectively integrate this skilled workforce could have significant social and economic repercussions." "- Our engineers must embrace resilience, long-term thinking, risk-taking, and a commitment to lifelong learning." "- By holding fast to universal humanistic values and the principle of *rahmatan l'il alamin*, we can guide Indonesia towards a sustainable and prosperous future." "" "My heartfelt thanks to the editor of The Jakarta Post for kindly publishing it in a timely manner and for supporting this series on the future of nuclear energy in Indonesia, and to DR Djarot Wisnubroto, Susetyo Hario, Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM)

"Cultural Dynamics and the Future of Nuclear Power in Indonesia," July 20, 2024: For those interested in Indonesia's energy future. This piece explores how our country's cultural values, political landscape, and technological considerations shape the discussion around nuclear energy." "" "The article examines various frameworks, including Hofstede’s dimensions of culture, Parson’s pattern variables, Kluckhohn & Strodtbeck’s value orientations, Rogers’ Innovation Diffusion Theory, and the three lenses framework often used in organizational studies (structural, political, and cultural perspectives). These frameworks help explain the factors influencing the acceptance and implementation of nuclear power in Indonesia. Despite the technological and environmental benefits, integrating nuclear power into our national energy mix remains a complex challenge." "" "I also highlight Indonesia's past success with mega projects, showcasing how unified political will can drive significant advancements. Such examples demonstrate that with strong leadership and cohesive efforts, Indonesia can overcome challenges and achieve ambitious goals." "" "A big thank you to The Jakarta Post for providing the platform to discuss this important issue. Your support in bringing this conversation to a wider audience is greatly appreciated." 2024-07-14 Contemplation on “Pengangguran Terbuka (Open Unemployment)”: Early on a serene Sunday morn...
Contemplation on “Pengangguran Terbuka (Open Unemployment)”: Early on a serene Sunday morning, while many residents are still enjoying the comfort of extended sleep after a long week of work, I find myself marveling at the beautiful landscape in a century-old area of Jakarta. The scene is picturesque, with leaves gently falling, reminiscent of autumn in the northern hemisphere. The walkways, shaded and expensive, are meticulously cleaned every morning by the diligent municipal crew. Yet, despite their efforts, these paths are marred by the pervasive smell of urine during the work weeks and are inundated with plastic garbage, leftover food, plastic containers, and cigarette butts. This idyllic setting has become a common rest area for a group of people from a certain industry, who spend much of their day outside. They are often seen resting, parking their vehicles, and spending time on their phones, contributing to the area’s litter and odors." "" "While the industry has provided flexible job opportunities and a source of income for many, it also brings challenges that need to be addressed. May be further ethnographic studies are needed to understand this phenomenon better and explore possible solutions. Some sectors have been hailed and praised as saviors, often claimed as providing jobs for the unemployed (“pengangguran”) and often bragged “pride of the country?” Really? Are they really employed?" "" "I don’t have the answer, especially if I see the definition of “pengangguran terbuka” by Badan Pusat Statistik *) as individuals who are part of the labor force but are not currently working, or THOSE WORKING IN JOBS THAT DO NOT MATCH THEIR SKILLS, EDUCATION, OR (DON’T MATCH THEIR) DESIRED EMPLOYMENT LEVEL (individu yang merupakan bagian dari angkatan kerja tetapi tidak bekerja saat ini, atau MEREKA YANG BEKERJA DALAM PEKERJAAN YANG TIDAK SESUAI DENGAN KETERAMPILAN, PENDIDIKAN, ATAU (TIDAK SESUAI DENGAN) TINGKAT PEKERJAAN YANG DIINGINKAN). If the definition is right, then they are still actually unemployed. " "" "If workers had been unemployed by one reason or another, by getting redundant from disrupted “padat karya” industries, bankrupt factories, from competing with younger workforce, or due to pressure to find more economic means to survive, moving to these so highly praised sectors made them remain unemployed (by BPS’ definition of “pengangguran terbuka”)." "" "Constructive dialogue and thoughtful solutions are needed to ensure that the industry can fulfill its promise of providing meaningful employment opportunities while also addressing the environmental and social challenges it brings." "" "*) Badan Pusat Statistik. (2023). Tingkat pengangguran terbuka (TPT) sebesar 5.32 persen dan rata-rata upah buruh sebesar 3.18 juta rupiah per bulan. Badan Pusat Statistik. Retrieved July 14, 2024, from https://lnkd.in/gR5Ns94b
2024-07-10 A friend recently shared an experience that left a lasting impression on him. Invited as a...
A friend recently shared an experience that left a lasting impression on him. Invited as an alumnus, he attended an MIT event, supposed to last from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM. After lunch, as he was busy preparing to take notes, he couldn’t help but tilt his head up to the speaker podium when the moderator introduced the next speaker, a lady professor, as the “Professor of Aeronautics and Astronautics.” The professor was Prof. Hamsa Balakrishnan the William E. Leonhard (1940) Professor at Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Her impressive background included a stint at the NASA Ames Research Center, a PhD from Stanford University, and a B.Tech. from the Indian Institute of Technology, Madras. Quoted from her official website “Her research, which focused on the design, analysis, and implementation of control and optimization algorithms for large-scale cyber-physical infrastructures, particularly air transportation systems, had garnered numerous awards. Her contributions included airport congestion control algorithms, air traffic routing and airspace resource allocation methods, machine learning for weather forecasts and flight delay prediction, and methods to mitigate environmental impacts. The audience was captivated by her expertise and accolades, including the NSF CAREER Award, the CNA Award for Operational Analysis, the AIAA Lawrence Sperry Award, the American Automatic Control Council's Donald P. Eckman Award, and several best paper awards”." "" "Such rich cultural capital, as described by Pierre Bourdieu’s four capital frameworks, brought back my friend’s childhood memories. In elementary and junior high school, many parents would encourage their children to study hard and perform well in school by saying, “Look at Dr. Karlina Laksono” (now Dr. Karlina Supelli) or “Look at Dr. Pratiwi” (referring to Dr. Pratiwi Sudarmono, the astronaut candidate). Dr. Karlina Laksono, an esteemed astronomer, was renowned for her contributions to the field. Her achievements inspired many to pursue science, and her dedication to astronomy set a high standard for academic excellence. Dr. Pratiwi Sudarmono, a microbiologist and one of NASA’s astronaut candidates from Indonesia, also stood out for her exceptional capabilities. Her selection as an astronaut candidate brought pride to many aspiring young scientists. Another admired figure was Margaret Thatcher. In addition to the admiration children had for their mothers, these women were significant role models." "" "Times have changed, and the current generation often looks up to wealth, beauty, and the fear of missing out as the criteria for admiration. Are the models primarily defined by materialistic and transient qualities? What values do these figures represent? Are they encouraging in-depth, resilience, and knowledge? " "" "Or perhaps let them be, as time will decide their future and the world’s future. To be fair, my generation is far from perfect either.
2024-07-10 In a recent conversation with Prof. Sanjay Sarma (now CEO of Asia School of Business), sev...
In a recent conversation with Prof. Sanjay Sarma (now CEO of Asia School of Business), several key insights on the future of education and learning were highlighted, reflecting a critical view on the current state of education and the need for transformative change." "" "A. Disproportionate Investment in Education: Prof. Sarma emphasized that traditional education systems need significant reform to stay relevant in the modern world. He compared the massive investments in artificial intelligence (AI)—$150 billion spent by companies, with future projections reaching $800 billion—to the GDP of Singapore, which stands at $500 billion. In contrast, the global spending on education is significantly lower, with education spending in 2022 being approximately $6 billion and projected to rise to only $8 billion by 2030. These figures highlight the vast scale and impact of AI investments and underscore the need for similar strategic investments in education to yield transformative results. However, current educational spending and approaches are not keeping pace, indicating a need for reevaluation of priorities and methods." "" "B. Structural Competition and Educational Paradigms: Education is described as being in the realm of structural competition. The outdated notion of a linear educational path—12 years of schooling followed by 4 years of higher education—was criticized as inadequate for preparing individuals for life, likening it to an ineffective gym routine. Instead, education should focus on developing lifelong learning skills and adaptability." "" "C. Reinventing Education (can be read as “reinventing learning): Prof. Sarma proposed several reforms to address the deficiencies in the current educational model:" "1) Pedagogy: Reinventing how subjects are taught to make learning more engaging and effective. Traditional lectures should be complemented with interactive, hands-on activities that foster deeper understanding *)." "2) Curriculum: Rethinking curricula to help both young and older learners climb up the intellectual stack. This involves integrating more meta-learning strategies, teaching students not just content but how to learn and adapt effectively **)." "3) Mode of Delivery: Changing the delivery methods to incorporate more technology and personalized learning experiences. Online instructional tools, when used appropriately, can be powerful allies, but they must be integrated thoughtfully to avoid becoming impediments ***)." "4) Social Contract: Redefining the societal expectations of education, recognizing that degrees have a "half-life" and that continuous learning and re-skilling are necessary in a rapidly changing world *)" "" "" "*) Chandler, D. L. (2020). A scientific approach to education reform. MIT News. Retrieved from https://lnkd.in/gRz26_Gs" "**) Sackstein, S. (2021). A Summary of Grasp: The Science of Transforming How We Learn. Retrieved from https://lnkd.in/gBFZVris" "***) Sarma, S., & Yoquinto, L. (2021). Grasp: The Science Transforming How We Learn.

2024-06-20 This is not a self-indulgent photoshoot, but rather a lesson I hope to share with my EL424...
This is not a self-indulgent photoshoot, but rather a lesson I hope to share with my EL4244 students. The photo captures a vibrant interaction outside a KFC Indonesia's outlet with enthusiastic crew members promoting a special meal bundle. The promotion, prominently displayed, offers a meal deal at 55,000 rupiah, including a pair of chicken pieces, a burger, and two Coca-Colas. After walking 5 kilometers under the hot Jakarta sun, this really caught my attention and sparked my interest and desire to buy some chicken." "" "Once inside, the enticing array of additional products caught my eye, and I ended up spending a total of 175,000 rupiahs. That initial 55,000 rupiah meal deal quickly led me to explore and indulge in other tempting items on the menu. As I was completing my purchase, something interesting happened. A resident from a nearby education hospital, dressed in a scrub suit, noticed my purchase. Intrigued by the attractive offer, he immediately called his fellow doctors across the street, urging them to come over for lunch. The word-of-mouth effect was powerful; his excitement demonstrated the impact of a well-crafted promotional bundle. The sight of a good deal and the positive reaction it generated among potential customers underscored the effectiveness of KFC's pricing tactics." "" "The key takeaways from this experience are twofold. First, it highlights the art of creating value, as demonstrated by KFC's promotion to entice and engage customers effectively. This aligns with step 23 of the 24 Disciplined Entrepreneurship Framework, "The dogs will eat the dog food," underscoring the importance of understanding and meeting customer needs through market research and innovative value creation. Second, it emphasizes the crucial skill of capturing value by defining paying customers—a rare ability in the startup landscape where blitzscaling and valuation worship often take precedence. Understanding paying customers is essential, but it doesn't stop there for my students' journey in entrepreneurship." "" "Felix Oberholzer-Gee's framework on creating and capturing value offers valuable insights. Creating value involves offering products or services that customers find desirable and are willing to pay for. Capturing value ensures that the business retains a portion of that value as profit. " "" "My wish for students is not only to master the skill of creating value but also to excel in capturing value. Observing this in action at KFC highlights the ultimate goal for students: to develop the ability to create value effectively and then move beyond, exercising at their best the skill of capturing value. The KFC crew's approach demonstrates a deep appreciation for capturing customer interest and defining paying customers, rooted in primary market research and a keen understanding of customer desires.

2024-06-09 "Storytelling as a powerful means to instill morals in children": Dr. Karlina Supelli high...
"Storytelling as a powerful means to instill morals in children": Dr. Karlina Supelli highlighted this during Dr. Johan Hasan's thesis defense at Sekolah Tinggi Filsafat Driyarkara. Her statement about the importance of storytelling in childhood education resonated deeply with me, underscoring the profound connection between our ideas. The timing couldn't have been more perfect, coinciding with my plan to present her with my book, "Discipline Storytelling," in person." "" "The legend of "Lutung Kasarung" embodies the rich cultural heritage of Sundanese people, yet its profound messages are often lost in today's fast-paced world. This sacred story, which once held great spiritual significance, was brought into the spotlight during the defense. This narrative, rich in themes of compassion, inner beauty, and the triumph of good over evil, was historically recited with mantras to ward off misfortune. By engaging with its moral lessons, individuals sought to attract positive energy and repel negative influences." "" "However, modernization and urbanization have led to the decline of these traditional rituals. Although "Lutung Kasarung" remains a cherished part of Sundanese folklore, its ritualistic aspects are now less commonly observed." "" "Dr. Supelli referenced this legend to frame a broader philosophical discussion. She quoted Martha Nussbaum and Charles Taylor on why teaching good principles often fails to produce moral change. Nussbaum argues that without engaging emotions and imagination, ethical teachings fall short. Taylor emphasizes that moral growth is deeply rooted in cultural and narrative contexts; without this connection, teaching remains ineffective." "" "Alasdair MacIntyre, renowned for his work in moral and political philosophy, particularly his concepts of "narrative" and "tradition," adds another layer to this discourse. He contends that moral truths are embedded in and understood through narratives and traditions rather than being universal or historical truths. Philosophers thus suggest that teaching morals through storytelling from early childhood can be more impactful." "" "Education through storytelling in childhood, which Dr. Supelli analogizes to the practice of "discernment,", is a powerful means to implant values, shaping the synaptic connections that define who we become. As per my research, it was clear that every child forms a mental model during the synaptic pruning period, influenced by their exposures and sparkling moment, "you are what your synaptic neurons process have made you"." "" "On a personal reflective note: This moment of meeting with Dr. Supelli was particularly meaningful. 35 years ago, I frequently read Dr. Karlina's newspaper columns and even once visited her campus to explore the astronomy department as a potential future venture. She was one of my role models, alongside other scientists, although I ultimately pursued nuclear engineering. Reflecting on it now, reading her columns was perhaps a premonition of who I am today.
2024-06-09 There is always a first time in life for everything: for enlightenment, for revelation. Th...
There is always a first time in life for everything: for enlightenment, for revelation. This was evident during the thesis defense of Dr. Johan Hasan from Universitas Ciputra Surabaya. The event, held at Sekolah Tinggi Filsafat Driyarkara, was a significant moment where I learned from the questions raised by eight prominent Indonesian philosophers, as well as the answers provided by the promovendus." "" "Proficiat to Dr. Johan Hasan on his inauguration and successful defense of his thesis entitled "Moral Education by L. Kohlberg and its Relevances for Pancasila Moral Education."*). I am grateful for the invitation to this important occasion and for the opportunity to share insights inspired by a poignant letter by Dr. Haim Ginott, a holocaust advisor: " "" "“Dear Teacher," "" "I am a survivor of a concentration camp. My eyes saw what no man should witness. Gas chambers built by learned engineers. Children poisoned by educated physicians. Infants killed by trained nurses. Women and babies shot and burned by high school and college graduates." "" "So, I am suspicious of education. My request is: Help your students become human. Your efforts must never produce learned monsters, skilled psychopaths, educated Eichmanns. Reading, writing, arithmetic are important only if they serve to make our children more human.”**)" "" "This letter serves as a bold reminder of the moral responsibilities inherent in education. It raises crucial questions about why communities, regardless of their religious devotion, sometimes struggle to uphold universal moral standards. This is evident in the widespread issues of corruption, human rights violations, injustice, and discrimination that can be found across various societies." "" "Dr. Johan Hasan’s research on moral education highlights the importance of fostering not just intellectual growth but also ethical and humane behavior. As educators and members of society, we must ensure that education cultivates compassion, empathy, and moral integrity, preventing the emergence of "learned monsters" and instead nurturing truly humane individuals." "" "*) Hasan, J. (2024). Moral education by L. Kohlberg and its relevances for Pancasila moral education (Doctoral dissertation). Sekolah Tinggi Filsafat Driyarkara, Jakarta." "**)Saldinger, A. G. (2001). Life in a Nazi concentration camp (1st ed., p. 12). Lucent Books.

2024-06-06 Did you know that vision might have been the spark that ignited the Cambrian Explosion, le...
Did you know that vision might have been the spark that ignited the Cambrian Explosion, leading to the rapid diversification of life forms 541 million years ago? Andrew Parker’s book, In the Blink of an Eye, fascinated me with this theory, suggesting that the advent of vision heightened predator-prey dynamics, accelerating global diversification during what was otherwise a silent and serene Cambrian period. These intensified interactions remind me of modern parallels in technology and business, where innovations create competitive situations akin to evolutionary arms races. For me, this underscores the utmost importance of sense-making, the ability to have advanced information at hand, and the execution to use that information effectively." "" "This book was introduced during a unique networking event called "Members Meet Members," which cleverly piggybacked on the popular Restaurant Week, a segment of Singapore Restart Week Spring Winners 2024. The networking was structured into several small gatherings over a few weeks, each dinner limited to eight people at renowned restaurants. The per-person cost was announced in advance, adding to my sense of security. My confidence was further boosted when I recognized a familiar face in the group—a fellow affiliated alumni of the MIT Sloan School of Management." "" "The intimate setting allowed for more meaningful connections. The group was diverse and fascinating, genuine and humble, sharing their experiences without any hint of arrogance: a second-generation Chinese-American from the West Coast, a Berkeley Chemistry major where many elements are named after their university; first-generation Chinese immigrants who graduated from both Harvard Business School and MIT in the early 1970s, now settled in China and Singapore; a Japanese national from the University of Tokyo with international living experience; a shipping engineer turned banker; a Malaysian-origin businessman in Singapore with a passion for culture; and two accomplished civil servants with bright futures." "" "Our conversations often veered into scientific discussions. One such discussion was about the book. Intrigued, I downloaded the e-book and started reading it. Over three weeks, I slowly buried into its dense and fascinating content. The book resonated deeply with me as it intertwines geology with rapid evolutionary changes, illustrating how a small change in vision can drive geological-scale transformations. " "" "Thanks Ms. Hau Yee Ng of MIT Club of Singapore , Dexter Tan Shuijian, Loh Ching Soo, Wenhao Xu, Michael T. Chang, xxx (not tagged for privacy reasons), Mr. Eugene Lee
2024-06-06 Discovering Leadership Presence in such an Extremely High Power Distance Index (PDI) Conte...
Discovering Leadership Presence in such an Extremely High Power Distance Index (PDI) Context" "" "Recently, my batch (Thomas Airlangga, Catherine Patinah, Endyas Pratitajati, D. Sadeli and A. Tobing et al) had the privilege of meeting with our leader, followed by a delightful lunch and an engaging exchange of messages. This experience left us impressed with his unique leadership style, offering valuable insights into leadership presence within an extreme 98% PDI environment. " "" "In such high PDI cultures, leadership norms typically emphasize maintaining a clear hierarchical structure. Leaders often create layers of screening and operate within a “bubble,” where messages are relayed through intermediaries or bureaucratic channels. This approach helps preserve the status quo and reinforces the leader’s authority. However, this leader’s approach presented a refreshing contrast to these traditional norms." "" "What’s particularly remarkable is how he manages to maintain respect and authority while being approachable and friendly. In high PDI contexts, such behavior could easily be misinterpreted as a weakness, leading subordinates to look down on the leader. However, he ensures that his friendliness is not perceived as a lack of strength by *consistently demonstrating competence, decisiveness, and fairness in his actions*. By making well-considered decisions and showing a clear vision, he reinforces his position of authority while fostering a supportive environment." "" "Despite the hierarchical expectations, he engaged with us informally, demonstrating a keen interest in building personal relationships and investing in our academic and personal growth. Instead of relying on intermediaries or bureaucratic layers, he acted directly, consulting with his team and making timely decisions based on collective input and his judgment. This was a striking departure from the norm and showcased a different side of leadership presence." "" "Moreover, we found that he dares to be vulnerable—a characteristic often seen in great leaders who challenge the status quo. This vulnerability, paired with his relational approach, demonstrates a different kind of strength, one that builds deeper trust and connection with his team." "" "This leads to an intriguing question: does his leadership style have anything to do with his upbringing and synaptic pruning during his childhood, adolescence, or youth? Perhaps the experiences and “sparkling moments” he encountered in his early life shaped his approach to leadership, enabling him to navigate high PDI expectations with a unique blend of authority and approachability." "" "It’s fascinating to see how effective leadership presence can break the mold in a high PDI environment. Wishing everyone the best as they work on their proposals and explore these dynamic aspects of leadership!

2024-05-26 Reflective Time: Revisiting the first lecture in the Research Proposal course by Prof. Yos...
Reflective Time: Revisiting the first lecture in the Research Proposal course by Prof. Yos Sunitiyoso, delivered by the esteemed Prof. Stephan Onggo, a closure. " "" "🚴‍♂️ We heard the expression, “Students don’t care how much you know until they know how much you care.” I truly felt this in class. Prof. Onggo showed he cared by preparing a session uniquely tailored for each of us in the Doctoral of Science in Management (DSM-9) program at the School of Business and Management ITB. He was the first to accurately present our research domains, objectives, and methods. He even read our early-stage research proposals! Perhaps because he was a guest professor, he didn’t take things for granted. Kudos to Prof. Sunitoyoso who organized this: he cares." " " "🚴‍♀️ “KISS” - “Keep It Simple S _ _p _ d”:" "• Last semester, we started with a single, shaky research question, which ballooned into 3 to 5 questions, each spawning more sub-questions. It was a tough time. Then, Prof. Onggo politely challenged us to reduce those confusing questions to a “UNIFIED RESEARCH QUESTION,” one sentence to represent all the sub-questions. Voila! This helped me find focus. What a "Simple but not Simpler" caveat. " "• Often, we dive into details and lose sight of the bigger picture. Writing the research methodology chapter became about answering “how will the data be collected” and “how will the data be analyzed.” This simplicity brought clarity and helped me appreciate my work on research philosophies more, eventually leading to the creation of my research flow chart." " " "🚵‍♀️ Reductionist vs. Holistic Systems Approaches:" "The magic of “system dynamics thinking” lies in breaking down large problems into manageable pieces while realizing they’re part of a much larger, complex system." "" "What’s next? Well, for now, I’m just savoring this reflective time. Cherishing the moment is an art form, after all. So, if you need me, I’ll be here, deep in thought, probably with a cup of coffee, pondering the mysteries of the universe…or just procrastinating on my next research chapter. Same difference, right? 😁 " "" "Have a good writing season: Arisona Lestari, Thomas Airlangga, Rosa Permata Sari, Endyas Pratitajati, Catherine Patinah, Rio Adrianto
2024-05-25 Excited to share an insight from the Closing Semester Class of Doctoral of Science in Mana...
Excited to share an insight from the Closing Semester Class of Doctoral of Science in Management - 9 in School of Business and Management ITB by Prof. Yos Sunitiyoso." "" "📝 “Write what we do, and do what we write” - Rama Permana PhD, quoting the importance of research journaling from his many colleagues. " "" "I find that reflexive thinking has helped me ensuring to be aware of my influence on the research process and outcomes. I have heard this advise so often and find it true:" "" "1. Acknowledging Personal Biases: I must recognize and disclose my biases and perspectives. This transparency enhances the credibility and authenticity of the research. Keeping a reflexive journal helps document thoughts, decisions, and changes in perspective over time. Reflect on why certain choices were made and how personal experiences might influence these choices." "" "2. Iterative Reflection: Reflexive thinking is not a one-time activity but an iterative process that should occur at all stages of the research. Regularly revisiting research questions, methodologies, and interpretations ensures they remain aligned with the evolving understanding of the topic. Set aside dedicated time after SOTA, after research proposal, after data collection, after analysis, to reflect on the process and any new insights gained." "" "3. Dialogical Engagement: Engaging in dialogues with peers, supervisors, and other researchers helps in gaining different perspectives and refining my own thinking. Participate in academic discussions, present work at conferences, and seek feedback from various sources to challenge and enhance reflexive thinking." "" "4. Ethical Considerations: I must consider how my work affects participants, communities, and the broader field of study. I learn to document ethical dilemmas and decisions in the research journal, explaining how they were addressed and the rationale behind these decisions." "" "5. Integration into Writing: Reflexive thinking should be evident in the dissertation itself. Discussing reflexivity in the methodology section can provide context to the research approach and justify the methods used. I will include a section on reflexivity, detailing how my background, experiences, and interactions have influenced the research process and findings." "" "Further Reading: " "• Throne, R. (2019). Autoethnography and Heuristic Inquiry for Doctoral-Level Researchers: Emerging Research and Opportunities. ICI-Global." "• Ellys, C. (2003). The Ethnographic I: A Methodological Novel about Autoethnography. AltaMira Press." "• Berger, R. (2015). “Now I see it, now I don’t: Researcher’s position and reflexivity in qualitative research.” Qualitative Research, 15(2), 219-234." "• Denzin, N. K., & Lincoln, Y. S. (2013). Collecting and Interpreting Qualitative Materials (4th ed.). Sage Publications. " "" "Thomas Airlangga, Rio Adrianto, Rosa Permata Sari, Catherine Patinah, Arisona Lestari, Endyas Pratitajati - all the best.

2024-05-21 "Foreign policy begins at home." - His Excellency dr. Vivian Balakhrisnan, Minister of For...
"Foreign policy begins at home." - His Excellency dr. Vivian Balakhrisnan, Minister of Foreign Affairs Republic of Singapore (2015-present)" "" "Reflect it to my dissertation, I envision applying that analogy to a home setting! Early childhood education, good parenting, a psychologically safe home, nutritious food, and jobs for parents are all crucial ingredients in creating a life long learner generation and a contributing to society citizen." "" "Additionally, I consulted ChatGPT and Microsoft Co-pilot (both of which can make mistakes!), “the effectiveness and success of a country's foreign policy are deeply rooted in its domestic conditions.”, so it means." "" "1. **Economic Strength:**" " - A robust and resilient domestic economy provides the resources needed to engage in effective foreign policy." " - Economic stability at home allows for greater investment in diplomatic initiatives, defense capabilities, and international aid." "" "2. **Political Stability:**" " - Political stability and good governance within a country enhance its credibility and reliability as an international partner." " - Strong, transparent institutions and the rule of law at home bolster a nation's ability to promote and uphold these values abroad." "" "3. **Social Cohesion:**" " - A united and cohesive society fosters a strong national identity and resilience against external pressures." " - Social harmony and integration support a positive global image and enhance the country’s soft power." "" "4. **Human Capital:**" " - Education and the development of human capital are crucial for producing skilled diplomats, negotiators, and international business leaders." " - Investing in human capital at home ensures a knowledgeable and capable workforce to advance national interests globally." "" "5. **Technological Advancement:**" " - Innovation and technological progress at home can enhance a country's competitive edge on the international stage." " - Technological leadership can be leveraged in international negotiations and economic partnerships." "" "6. **Infrastructure and Resources:**" " - Developing strong infrastructure and managing resources efficiently at home can support international trade and economic diplomacy." " - Adequate infrastructure at home ensures the smooth functioning of international business operations and logistics." "" "7. **Public Support:**" " - Public understanding and support for foreign policy initiatives are crucial for their success." " - Engaging and educating the domestic population about foreign policy goals can build a broad base of support and legitimacy." "" "Apparently, the phrase “Foreign policy begins at home” can be considered a fundamental principle of foreign policy, often taught in introductory courses. The internal health and strength of a nation lay the foundation for its ability to conduct effective and impactful foreign policy. Ensuring stability, prosperity, and unity at home enables a country to project its influence and values abroad more effectively.

2024-05-15 PREVALENT BIASES WHEN INVESTING: lessons from Theranos' Case: (This post was removed by L...
PREVALENT BIASES WHEN INVESTING: lessons from Theranos' Case:  (This post was removed by LinkedIn, but I decide to re-post after revising some aspect that may have been deemed as reasons for removal, after sit-in in a class in MIT last month where they used Theranos as a case study to discuss involvement of ethics in MVBP). " "" "Quoting from Pitchbook (https://lnkd.in/ddYUB53z), " "" ""So where are those investors now? And what strategy or funding style have they deployed in the aftermath of the Theranos scandal? PitchBook data shows that just a few of the VC firms backing Theranos have gone on to fund medtech startups in the years since late 2015, when the company began to implode.  " "" "1. Only healthcare-focused hedge fund PFM  and DA subsequently stepped up their bets on healthcare devices.  " "2. Some Theranos backers, like AV and DFJ (which later rebranded as TV), found continued success through a series of winning tech investments—but all of those were spread across non-medical categories.  " "3. Other firms are no longer in business for various reasons, such as early investors JP, AV and TV" *)" "" "Are all VCs bad? NO not at all ! Many impactful investor/ VCs have much more noble goal than merely "2.5% X TENURE X Disbursed Fund+ 20% carry". VCs have been instrumental in enhancing the quality of life in planet earth. " "" "Yes, Irrational Decision: unfortunately, this notorious Theranos case may emphasize the importance of applying a rigorous methodology in screening startups to ensure biases against irrational decision that is very prevalent among us are minimized. *)" " " "1. Human favor simple-looking options and complete information over complex, ambiguous options hence : information bias, ambiguity bias, belief bias, conjunction fallacy, Occam's razor. " "2. We favor the immediate, relatable thing in front of us to stay focused hence : appeal to novelty bias, hyperbolic discounting bias, identifiable victim effect bias. " "3. we need to act fast: must be confident that we are impactful and feel what we do is important, hence: fundamental attribution error bias, trait ascription bias, actor-observer bias, self-serving bias, ilustroy superiority bias, Dunning-Kruger effect bias, optimism bias, overconfidence bias. " "4. We imagine things and people we're familiar with or fond of as better, hence halo effect, in-group bias, cheerleader effect, out-group homogeneity bias, positivity effect, well-travelled road effect" "5. We fill in characteristics from stereotypes, generalities, and prior history: hence bandwagon effect, authority bias, moral credential effect, stereotyping bias, group attribution error.  " "" "*https://lnkd.in/ddYUB53z" "**)from Cognitive Bias Codex, 2016. " "Picture credit to Dall-E
2024-05-14 My 54th birthday in May coincided with a full day of PhD classes in School of Business and...
My 54th birthday in May coincided with a full day of PhD classes in School of Business and Management ITB with other future PhDs: Rio Adrianto , Thomas Airlangga , Endyas Pratitajati , Arisona Lestari , Rosa Permata Sari and Prof. Dermawan Wibisono. The leader of the class Dr. Catherine Patinah surprised me on behalf of the class with a birthday cake, making me feel special and appreciated. Their kindness contrasted with the challenges I faced over the past year, including betrayal, bullying, misunderstandings, and discrimination. Despite these hardships, their care provided a light of hope and strength." "" "I received birthday greetings from many people, including robotic messages from various loyalty programs such as Qatar Airways “Privilege Club,” Garuda Indonesia Airways “Fly Garuda,” Harvard Alumni Association, The Harvard/MIT Cooperative Society, Cartier, The Pakubuwono Development, Singtel, Panin Dai-ichi Life, and the MIT Club of Indonesia (Kak Hillman Akil). These messages, either personally crafted or automated, reminded me of the connections and affiliations I have formed over the years to which I feel lucky to experience them. " "" "Strangely, these bountiful greetings arrived after an anticlimactic end to my long relationship with Singapore Airlines, flown with them since 1994 and had been a PPS member for the last 10 years. Now, it is over, and I am left with a sense of bitterness over how it ended. The loyalty and dedication I showed seemed overshadowed by an abrupt and cold termination of our association, adding to my feelings of disillusionment, that I promised not to spend any more money with them again. " "" "Nevertheless, I reflect on the support I have received during my birthday. The acts of kindness and heartfelt messages from my friends reminded me of the resilience and strength that community can provide." "" "In reflection, I found solace and mindfulness through an ancient prayer, adapted to express my gratitude and hopes: "Our Father, Your wisdom and power are beyond my understanding, and I trust in your guidance. Help me to align my actions with your will and to contribute to the fulfillment of your kingdom. Provide for my needs and give me the strength and resources to face each day. Thank you for the blessings of health, relationships, and financial stability that sustain me. I ask for your help in dealing with those who have betrayed me, looked down on me, and wished for my failure and suffering. Give me the strength to forgive them and the wisdom to navigate these relationships. Protect me from their negativity and help me to stay focused on your path for me. Fill my heart with peace and my mind with clarity so that I can rise above any hurt or anger. For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. Amen."" "" "This ancient prayer, Amidah and the Lord’s Prayer, adapted to my personal journey, serves as a reminder of the power of mindfulness and the strength that comes from a supportive community.

2024-04-28 I had the honor of reuniting with Professor Stefan Thomke this week, just days after celeb...
I had the honor of reuniting with Professor Stefan Thomke this week, just days after celebrating the fifth anniversary of my participation in GMP-26 at Harvard Business School. Happy 5th anniversary to all 135 or so dear GMP26 friends! Our nearly two-hour conversation in a cozy coffee shop near his weekend home was an enlightening exploration of the concept of 'luck'—where preparation meets opportunity and action." "" "Professor Thomke’s journey was profoundly shaped by formative influences from an early age, including his supportive parents and grandparents, a transformative ninth-grade physics teacher, and his encouraging wife. These foundational mentors deeply influenced his early perspectives and approach. Building on this solid foundation, later academic mentors like Eric Von Hippel played pivotal roles in his career. Professor Thomke shared how his interactions with Von Hippel, during his multidisciplinary studies at Massachusetts Institute of Technology, culminated in the completion of his PhD in Electrical Engineering, which had been his original intent, significantly influenced his career trajectory, pivoting from a high-profile consulting role toward a profound position as a professor at HBS. This transition showcases how preparedness can transform unexpected opportunities into defining moments." "" "Our discussion focused on the creation of one’s fortune through resilience and readiness. Key insights included the importance of recognizing 'lucky breaks,' which can turn challenges into opportunities with the right mindset. Professor Thomke highlighted the virtues of humility, adhering to principles, engaging with insightful and compassionate individuals, and consistently aiming for excellence—even when it goes unnoticed. Not to mention the discipline of having “fun” (of course not comprising the highest quality of your delivery). " "" "He underscored the importance of hanging around with those who recognize quality and the crucial role of mentors who not only command respect but also provoke growth. " "" "On a personal note, I am grateful that Professor Thomke, a role model whose humility and wisdom continue to inspire, graciously accepted a copy of my recently published book, “Disciplined Storytelling?” (https://a.co/d/1SwRBUe in Amazon) designed for my engineering students. I didn’t have time to go to see his electric Porsche AG but had a good look at the classic A. Lange & Söhne on his wrist! " "" "This unique reunion was not merely about reminiscing but also about reinforcing the values that guide our professional paths. Meeting with Professor Thomke on April 27, 2024—five years after my graduation—underscored my growth and learning and reinvigorated my commitment to the reason I studied in that institution in the first place.
2024-04-27 I recently had the pleasure of reconnecting with Professor Jason Jay on campus, a pivotal ...
I recently had the pleasure of reconnecting with Professor Jason Jay on campus, a pivotal figure in my academic journey. Professors John Sterman, Roberto Rigobon and Zeynep Ton, alongside Professor Jay, co-taught the course ‘Strategies for Sustainable Business’ during my time at MIT Sloan School of Management. That day 19 October 2016, initially, I wondered if I had wandered into the wrong classroom, as the curriculum’s strong emphasis on environmental sustainability and climate technology was uncharted territory for me. However, it was through engaging simulations like ‘Fishbanks’ that I found a profound connection to the subject, ultimately inspiring me to become an En-ROADS Simulation Climate Interactive Ambassador. " "" "The course taught me to approach complex issues by avoiding a holier-than-thou attitude and instead emphasizing effective communication and collaboration. This mindset was further reinforced by Professor Jay’s insightful book, “Breaking Through Gridlock: The Power of Conversation in a Polarized World,” which I read subsequently." "" "This week, I had the honor of revisiting these valuable lessons with Professor Jay and sharing my recently published book, “Disciplined Storytelling,” (https://a.co/d/1SwRBUe in Amazon) designed for my engineering students, presenting him with the autographed copy. " "" "I am excited about the prospect of learning more from him in the future and continuing to explore the intersections of sustainability and strategic communication." "" "Photo credit to another Sloanie and system change agent Hanson Gong. Good to see him again.
2024-04-27 Reunited with Prof. John Sterman: In June 2016, I embarked on the first of sixteen courses...
Reunited with Prof. John Sterman: In June 2016, I embarked on the first of sixteen courses at the MIT Sloan Executive Education, starting with a week-long intensive course on System Dynamics delivered by Professor John Sterman. This series of courses ultimately earned me affiliated alumni status at MIT Sloan School of Management. The initial course explored crucial concepts such as structure determining behavior, policy resistance, feedback loops, balancing and reinforcing processes, the non-linear nature of life, unintended consequences, and the complexities of large, interdependent systems. While these principles resonated with those I had encountered in nuclear reactor dynamics, Professor Sterman brought a fresh and impactful perspective to them." "" "Today, I had the honor of meeting him once more just before he delivered a compelling ten-minute speech at the MIT Sustainability Summit: Systems Change as the Founder of MIT Sloan Sustainability Initiative. He graciously accepted a copy of my recently published book, "Disciplined Storytelling." (https://a.co/d/1SwRBUe in Amazon) designed for my engineering students. I am deeply grateful." "" "Thanks Saman Baghestani for the picture.
2024-04-27 Meeting Professor Peter Senge today was a direct connection to the roots of system dynamic...
Meeting Professor Peter Senge today was a direct connection to the roots of system dynamics, a field passionately advanced by his mentor, Professor Jay Forrester at MIT. During his session, Professor Senge shared insights that transcend conventional measures of success, notably reflecting on the quote, " "" "‘You will never get enough of what you don’t need to make you happy,’ attributed to Eric Hoffer. " "" "He emphasized that true happiness and intellectual growth are not merely a result of being smarter or accumulating material wealth. His teachings in ‘The Fifth Discipline’ advocate for a holistic approach, focusing on emotional intelligence, purposeful work, and systemic thinking to achieve sustainable personal and organizational development. " "" "This memorable encounter was further highlighted by his gracious act of autographing a book written by Professor Forrester (Principles of system dynamics, : text and woorkbokk Chapter 1-10) symbolizing the profound intellectual lineage and the enduring impact of their work in system dynamics.

I had the privilege of collaborating with Dr. Desi Utami, of Faculty of Agriculture, Universitas Gadjah Mada, on learning "how to transform a scholarly paper into an opinion / academia section in magazine or newspaper." This initiative specifically focuses on crafting compelling opinion pieces for serious magazines or daily newspapers, aimed at offering value-based ideas and opinions to an educated audience. Such articles are not about achieving the highest technical quality, providing exhaustive details, explanations, or the most accurate research data. Neither are they designed to be the simplest to read, nor do they always represent the latest in current events." "" "However, these articles are meticulously crafted, representing a synthesis of knowledge that has been accumulated over significant time, resources, and effort. They present reasoned, albeit subjective, viewpoints and are deeply rooted in values. It is essential to highlight the sophistication of this genre; treating these carefully constructed narratives as unworthy of serious consideration or as pseudo-science not only misjudges their value but also shows a profound level of arrogance. Such a rejection overlooks the effort, thought, and value these narratives contribute to public discourse, offering nuanced, well-considered perspectives that significantly enrich our collective understanding." 2024-03-12 "Travel is the fatal enemy of prejudice," remarked Mark Twain (Read: "Travel zaps prejudic...
"Travel is the fatal enemy of prejudice," remarked Mark Twain (Read: "Travel zaps prejudice,"),probably while paddling a raft or charming his way across continents. But here's the twist: not all wanderlust leads to wisdom. " "" "This essay, akin to a quirky travelogue, ventures into the curious case of why gallivanting around the globe doesn't always scrub the grime of prejudice off every traveler." "" "Imagine, if you will, a tourist so wrapped up in their mental luggage—packed with hefty biases and stiff attitudes—that no amount of exotic destinations can unfold their minds. We're about to take a detour through the brain's back alleys, guided by the trusty map of Cognitive Dissonance Theory, to see why some travelers' prejudices cling to them like stubborn suitcase stickers, despite the most eye-opening encounters." "" "With a magnifying glass on various culture theories (shoutout to Parsons, Trompenaars, and Hofstede for their brainy contributions), we'll dive into a case study that feels more like a reality TV show: "The Real World: Culture Shock Edition." It features individuals taking not just a gap year but decades to shake off the culture shock blues." "" "So, buckle up—or, more aptly, unbuckle your mind belts—as we explore the scenic route to understanding why travel, the supposed prejudice-exterminator, sometimes misses the mark. And remember, it's not just about the stamps in your passport but the flexibility in your thoughts that counts." "" "Travel does not automatically reduce prejudice, because travelers may interpret unfamiliar experiences through pre-existing beliefs that preserve rather than challenge bias.

2024-03-09 In the grand virtual masquerade ball that is the internet, some introverts don a digital m...
In the grand virtual masquerade ball that is the internet, some introverts don a digital mask and dance into the world of extroversion with surprising agility. It's as if the online realm casts a spell on them, transforming their usual cautious whisper into a confident shout across the digital rooftops. This phenomenon, akin to watching a quiet librarian turn into a rockstar at a karaoke bar, raises eyebrows and questions alike. Why do these digital Jekyll and Hydes emerge once the safety net of a screen is in place?" "" "This curious shift is but one of four fascinating dance moves in the personality communication ballroom, standing out for its sheer unpredictability. Unlike its more predictable counterparts, this transformation sees introverts not just stepping out of their comfort zones but leaping out, fingers ablaze across keyboards, often outpacing the thoughtful pace at which their brains prefer to waltz through conversations in the physical world. This online haste can mirror the panic-stricken fluster of an introvert suddenly spotlighted in a face-to-face chat, leading to remarks that may dart out sharper and quicker than intended, sometimes leaving a trail of digital regret in their wake." "" "Interestingly, the digital world's curtain of anonymity and distance can embolden introverts to express themselves more freely, unshackled from the immediate weight of in-person reactions. However, this newfound freedom, while liberating, can sometimes veer into the territory of impulsiveness, where comments are fired off like hastily drawn arrows, missing the mark of intention and landing in the realm of unintended offense or misinterpretation." "Simultaneously, a curious subplot unfolds as some extroverts take a step back in this digital dance, adopting a more introverted stance online. Their quieter, more reflective online personas stand as commendable examples of adaptability, showcasing the nuanced spectrum of human interaction that the digital age beckons us to navigate." "" "This article wades into these waters, seeking to unravel the threads that weave together the fabric of our digital personas, illuminating the complex ballet of introversion and extroversion in the virtual and physical realms.

"" "Picture this: a jellyfish, bobbing along in the ocean, its life a model of serene simplicity, a stark contrast to the whirlwind of human existence. "" "This dialogue invites us to navigate the complexities of life, to safeguard our intellectual offspring, and to seek fulfillment not in external validation but in the essence of our contributions." 2024-03-08 Quiet Voices, Loud Ideas: The Introvert’s Guide to Success: In our clamorous world, where ...
Quiet Voices, Loud Ideas: The Introvert’s Guide to Success: In our clamorous world, where clamor often passes for clout, my recent exploration investigates into the subdued yet mighty force of introverts. Leveraging insights from Patrick Winston on storytelling's impact, alongside Maria Callas's musings on meticulous prep, I project into how introverted characteristics can pave the way for significant achievements." "" "This piece is a tribute to my pupils, many of whom are nurtured to embrace their introversion. The message is clear: There’s no need to morph into an extrovert; revel in your introverted uniqueness." "" "Here's a sneak peek: "Patrick Winston once insightfully noted, "Your chances of success are significantly influenced by your storytelling prowess, writing capabilities, and the caliber of your ideas, in that order." This statement might suggest a bias towards extroverted flair, but that’s a misread. Reflecting on time-honored sayings, we're reminded that "A word aptly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver," underscoring the might of measured speech and the value of a well-timed pitch—virtues that thrive not on outspokenness but through thoughtful practice and clarity. This resonates deeply with my students, introverts by nurture, hailing from cultures that traditionally shy away from outspoken self-expression. Yet, in digital dialogues, they occasionally don a mask of extroversion, a guise that may precipitate premature, sometimes harmful, exchanges."" "" "This leads to an enlightening proposition: Introversion does not hinder one's knack for weaving engaging narratives, assuming the ideas are compelling. As Maria Callas aptly highlighted, the essence of storytelling and communication "begins long before the curtain rises and continues well after its fall," spotlighting the supremacy of preparation and timing over personality type. Hence, the mastery of storytelling and the effective dissemination of ideas are not gifts reserved for the vocally vibrant but are accolades achieved through persistent effort, time, and dedication." "" "It's crucial, then, for us as educators and mentors, to champion an environment that empowers our youth, introverted or not, to hone these indispensable skills. By doing so, we validate that the power to influence, lead, and inspire isn't held solely by the most audible in the room but is within reach for anyone dedicated to perfecting the art of storytelling and the judicious sharing of their insights.

2024-03-02 The urge to immediately broadcast our thoughts, fueled by a craving for swift approval and...
The urge to immediately broadcast our thoughts, fueled by a craving for swift approval and accolades, has become a hallmark of contemporary culture. Everyone seems to be in a rush for endorsements, eager for affirmations like “you have a bright future,” “you can do it,” or “you are unique,” or "you are in a million". This relentless pursuit of instant validation often overshadows the importance of genuine engagement with others, be they educators, colleagues, hosts, guests, or investors. The repercussions are troubling, manifesting in increased feelings of isolation, mental health challenges, and a rise in self-centered attitudes. While establishing a direct causal relationship would require empirical research, these trends are unmistakable in my observations. The current approach to sharing and communicating is fraught with missteps, including premature elevator pitches and a heavy reliance on dialogues that fail to resonate. The push to be constantly heard and to lead conversations stands in stark contrast to the nuanced, often quiet, and harmonious ways of natural communication." "" "The narrative introduces a compelling juxtaposition: mastering the succinctness of an "elevator pitch" amidst silence. It emphasizes the need to strike a balance between the contemplative quietude of silence and the imperative to convey one's ideas crisply and impactfully in the brief encounters that define our era. Merging introspection with eloquence, this concept offers a fresh perspective on communication, advocating for a balance between reflective silence and proactive interaction." "" "Thanks the esteemed editor The Jakarta Post, especially Mr. Dwi Atmanto who kindly refined my writing and published it https://lnkd.in/g5NkZYCj on Saturday, 2 March 2024." "" "https://lnkd.in/gzC3E3BJ

Today, I join many in reflecting on the profound impact Professor Edward Roberts of the MIT Sloan School of Management, the very founder of Martin Trust Center for MIT Entrepreneurship has had on many lives. While I am deeply saddened by his passing, I am also incredibly grateful for the opportunity to have been one of the many students whose soul was touched by his warmth and genuine interest. " "" "During the MIT Entrepreneurship Development Program in 2017 and 2018 hosted by MIT Sloan Executive Education, I was fortunate enough to witness first-hand his grace and his unwavering energy. Professor Roberts was more than just an educator; he was a lighthouse of inspiration, encouraging us to pursue our passions with diligence and creativity. His significant contributions to the field of entrepreneurship and his dedication to his students have not only shaped the industry but have also played a pivotal role in my academic journey, especially in my dissertation work." "" "I cannot help today but reread his important book of his, "Entrepreneurs in High Technology," and found a handwritten inscribed autograph: " "" ""Dear Toro, Best wishes to you on your own dedicated efforts in entrepreneurship! Good luck, Ed Roberts"" "" "Since receiving that in 2018, the path I've traveled in entrepreneurship has been nothing short of historic. His encouraging words not only fueled my dedication but also marked the beginning of an extraordinary journey. What has transpired since then between me and the world of entrepreneurship is a testament to the profound influence of his words and belief in my potential. His legacy continues to inspire and guide me as I face the challenges and triumphs of creating innovation driven entrepreneurs within a minimal innovation ecosystem culture.
2024-02-28 Navigating the global scene today feels a bit like trying to get your point across in a no...
Navigating the global scene today feels a bit like trying to get your point across in a noisy, crowded room. Everyone's talking in different languages, from tech-speak to legalese, and here we are, trying to make an impact with more than just our impressive collection of emojis. But here's the kicker: rocking the communication game isn't just about throwing around big words in English (or any other language for that matter). It's about making those genuine connections that spark a lightbulb moment, fostering a "huh, I never thought of it that way" understanding, and maybe, just maybe, getting people to jump on your bandwagon." "" "Week 1: Introduction. This class isn't just another set of lecture on why you need to up your chat game. It's a nudge to remind you that whether you're aiming to be the next big thing in your organization or just trying to get through a family dinner without a debate on the merits of pineapple on pizza, how you communicate can either open doors or slam them shut (hopefully not on your foot)." "" "So, why should you care? Picture this: you're at the helm of a team, about to unveil an idea that could either be the next sliced bread or end up toasted. Or maybe you're about to expand your LinkedIn universe beyond your mom and your best friend from kindergarten. The way you toss your words around could either make you the captain of your ship or leave you stranded on a deserted island." "" "A remarkable lesson unfolded in the En-Roads UN-Summit Climate Interactive Simulation Workshop I held in Hwa Chong Institution in Singapore on 25 Jan https://lnkd.in/gmH7f7AR. "" "Their proposed action items, also examining the impacts of their policy measures, among others, are: stopping the construction of new coal power plants and reducing the capacity of existing ones, proposing an optimum carbon tax, formulating innovative strategies to enhance efficiency in buildings and transportation and proposing a dozen of invention ideas on carbon capture, carbon removal and carbon storage as well the several novel ideas on new form of energies, and deciding taxing or subsidizing what forms of energies, and proposing carbon pricing/tax. These are critical steps towards mitigating climate change, without point - finger, laying the blame on any industries, or promoting one single solution (none!)." " "" "NOW CONTRAST THIS with "What is a 'greenflation'?" infamous basic, buzzword-laden question posed in a nation-wide Vice Presidential debate. This raises concerns about the candidate's ability to lead a nation through complex, multifaceted issues, as it aligns only with a foundational level of understanding – the point where elementary school students start, not where they finish. 2024-01-24 "Preaching to the choir falls on deaf ears when the congregation seeks not truth, but vali...
"Preaching to the choir falls on deaf ears when the congregation seeks not truth, but validation." This expression poignantly illustrates a communication challenge today: valid and factual opinions may go unheeded in discussions where affirming personal beliefs overshadows the quest for objective truth." "" "For instance, debating a CNN article like "The next holy grail for EVs: Batteries free of nickel and cobalt" (https://lnkd.in/gNcmuMeq) to win younger audiences isn't just about presenting an opinion or establishing truth. Even well-founded opinions can be ignored if they conflict with prevailing views or personal interests or other noises. Speculative answers won't win them (https://lnkd.in/g6vPaNu7). It is a holy-grail, whoever predicts well, may hold the future: energy and its storage, hence only the CEO or his Chief R&D. Nobody else, not even kings or presidents or rulers. " "" "So, in a debate where the goal is to win the younger audiences' demography, several focused strategies have proven effective:" "" "1. Ask Our Opponent to Elaborate: Gently challenge our opponent to provide more details about their accusation, especially when we know it most likely is unfounded or provocative. E.g. “You’ve raised an interesting point about our team’s finding. Could you please elaborate on what specifically led you to this conclusion?” This demonstrates our willingness to engage and understand their perspective without getting defensive." "" "2. Maintain Composure and Confidence: Emphasize our composure and confidence throughout the exchange. Respond in a measured and controlled manner, highlighting that we are open to a constructive discussion. Our calm demeanor, as expected from much older and wiser leader, will convey professionalism and cool-headedness." "" "3. Avoid Technical Jargon: Keep our response clear and concise, avoiding technical details. Use straightforward language that is easily understood by all generations. E.g. “Let’s address this in a clear and straightforward manner…”" "" "4. Use Charismatic Communication: While avoiding humor, maintain a charismatic communication style. Engage our audience with concise and impactful statements. Our charisma should emanate from our composed and confident manner, again especially if we are much older, which can be appealing across generational gaps." "" "5. Redirect Focus to Our Strengths: After addressing the accusation, swiftly shift the conversation to our team’s strengths or achievements. E.g. “While we’re discussing this, it’s also a good opportunity to highlight why our team find that .... ”" "" "6. Conclude with a Positive Note: End on a positive and confident note, emphasizing our team’s commitment to growth and excellence. E.g. “We value constructive feedback as it helps us improve. We take pride in our team’s work and remain dedicated to continuous progress."" "" "Those have helped me. Not sure those will help others, since the mental model and purpose or raison d’être may be different.
