2021-09-12 Prof. Mike Roberto: “Many people complain about their daily or weekly schedule. Too many...
Prof. Mike Roberto: “Many people complain about their daily or weekly schedule. Too many meetings. Too much time spent fighting fires. Not enough opportunities to interact with customers and other external constituents. " "" "While these complaints may be justified, many of us don't take the opportunity to periodically engage in serious self-reflection about how we allocate our time. Leaders at all levels should make it a regular habit to examine their calendar and ask themselves a few questions:" "1. What types of activities are taking up most of my time?" "2. Are there some important activities that are not receiving sufficient attention?" "3. Who in the organization or outside the organization should I be spending more time with in the coming weeks and months?" "4. How can I build in some time into my calendar for broader strategic and long term thinking/planning?" "5. What activities do I need to reduce or even eliminate so as to make time for other important matters?" "6. Where in my schedule will I build in an opportunity for systematic, routine self-reflection, not just about the allocation of my time, but about other important aspects of my professional and personal life?" "" "In short, let's all stop complaining about our schedule and start doing something about it. Carve out the time needed to conduct critical work. Question 5, though, will be the most difficult one. We can't make time for crucial activities without taking some things off our plate. We have to give up some activities to make time for others.”

A temporary cooperation switchback applies when entrepreneurs want to self-commercialize but are initially blocked from doing so, often for lack of complementary assets. Here, the entrepreneur uses an initial cooperative strategy to gather the resources and expertise necessary to develop or acquire the needed complementary assets, which then enables product market entry." "2. A temporary competition switchback is essential for entrepreneurs who wish to cooperatively commercialize but find themselves either unable to do so due to partner uncertainty regarding the value of the innovation, or unwilling to do so given their limited ability to negotiate attractive agreements. In this case, entering the product market demonstrates the value of the technology, builds the brand, and develops other assets needed in order to eventually achieve favorable cooperative arrangements. " "" "Switchbacks thus initially adopt a non-ideal strategy that works to mitigate existing constraints, and thereby enables transitioning to the ideal strategy"" "" "Matt Marx., David H. Hsu., (June 2015), Strategic Switchbacks: Dynamic Commercialization Strategies for Technologies Entrepreneurs

In entrepreneurship teaching context : WHY THIS COUNTRY CULTURALLY CANNOT RELY ON SUCCESS STORY MODEL BUT NEED A ROBUST ENTREPRENEURSHIP FRAMEWORK THAT MONITOR/ MENTOR CLOSELY IN LEARNING THEM OR IMPLEMENTING THEM? "" "This impression is a very 50,000ft view, as Indonesia has more than 1,300 ethnic groups, and each has its own unique culture. " "" "Borrowing Hofstede's 6-D model, I presented 2 of 6 dimensions due to space limitation. For more complete analysis please refer to https://lnkd.in/gUbgyYD" "" "POWER DISTANCE" "" "Indonesia scores high on this dimension (score of 78) which means that the following characterises the Indonesian style: Being dependent on hierarchy, unequal rights between power holders and non power holders, superiors in-accessible, leaders are directive, management controls and delegates. Power is centralized and managers count on the obedience of their team members. Employees expect to be told what to do and when. Control is expected and managers are respected for their position. Communication is indirect and negative feedback hidden. High Power Distance also means that Indonesian co-workers would expect to be clearly directed by the boss or manager – it is the classic Guru-Student kind of dynamic that applies to Indonesia. Westerners may be considerably surprised with the visible, socially acceptable, wide and unequal disparity between the rich and poor ." "" "INDIVIDUALISM" "" "Indonesia, with a low score of (14) is a Collectivist society. This means there is a high preference for a strongly defined social framework in which individuals are expected to conform to the ideals of the society and the in-groups to which they belong. One place this is visible clearly is in the aspect of the Family in the role of relationships. For example, In Indonesia, if one wishes to marry, it is important to meet a woman’s family because the family is so important to her. If a man wants to be taken seriously by a woman, he has to visit the latter’s family and introduce himself formally to the parents of the girl. It is inappropriate to court a woman and formalize the relationship without informing the parents of the girl first. Another example of collectivist culture of Indonesia is in the equation between child and parent" "" "Indonesian children are committed to their parents, as are the parents committed to them all their growing lives. Their desire is to make their parents’ life easier. There is a desire to take care of parents and give them support in their old age. There is an Asian saying that is accepted in Indonesia, “You can get another wife or husband but not another mother or father”. This family loyalty is also apparent in the fact that Indonesian families keep elders (such as grandparents) at home instead of sending them to any institution. In Individualist societies the focus is on the nuclear family only.

How many so-called #platforms (read: hype platforms) die prematurely or die within < year? Many if not MOST of them. RIBBON CUTTING CEREMONY". " "" ""It normally starts with a group / department in an established organization (either for profit or not for profit) who comes up with an idea of #digitalplatforms . Then they make glossy presentations to their leaders and they get the budget to start working. Then comes the big ceremonial day: they invite media (TV, radios, social media, press), VIPs (central government officers, head of organizations, local government, etc). This is not just an internal event, and normally everyone claims this is going to be the next "it" platform" " "" ""Once the ceremony is over, the team build the platform, bring the right supplier, create a beautiful website, find right integrators, set up the system and they launch it. They may have some participants, but there are no interactions most of the time"" "" ""Unless you need this for publicity or political campaign, yes you can take this approach. "2. together with customers and such a complimenting skills/networks and same objective team, providing the fit solution / MVP / Customer Journey and high level spec. Keep experimenting or testing. " "3. Focusing on the Cost of customer acquisition and keep experimenting before they prototype. They make a good pitch, and keep their company afloat before reaching the next milestone. " "" "Be grateful and humble if you are very smart. You are needed in a team of founders. Please find cofounders who can help round out the skills and knowledge leading the company. "" ""I have never let my schooling interfere with my education" - Mark Twain" "" "Further, late Noble Laurette Professor Richard Feynman once quoted, "Never confuse education with intelligence. Intelligence isn't the ability to remember and repeat, like they teach you in school. Intelligence is the ability to learn from experience, solve problems, and use our knowledge to adapt to new situations"" "" "1. Smart people sometimes devalue other skills, like relationship building, and over-concentrate on intellect. Very smart people sometimes see their success as inevitable because of their intellect, and don’t see other skills as important." "2. Teamwork can be frustrating for very smart people. When someone grasps concepts quickly and has high standards for their own performance it can create difficulties when working with others who take longer to process information and pick up concepts." "3. Smart people often attach a lot of their self-esteem to being smart, which can decrease their resilience and lead to avoidance. If a lot of your self-esteem rests on your intelligence, it can be very difficult to be in situations that reveal chinks in your armor. " "4. Smart people get bored easily. " "5. Smart people sometimes see in-depth thinking and reflection as the solution to every problem." "" "Point 1-5 are extracted from: Alice Boyes, 5 Ways Smart People Sabotage Their Success, Harvard Business Review, 13 November 2018. Print
2021-06-13 My humble key recommendations "What to do for the SMEs-98% group"- written for a friend in...
My humble key recommendations "What to do for the SMEs-98% group"- written for a friend in public office: " "" "1. Start with Paying Customer : Conduct a thorough study in inventorizing general trends of paying customers and unique trend of paying customers in in the kompleks/sektor jalan/ kelurahan/ kecamatan/ kabupaten" "" "2. Prioritizing Local Domicile in procuring simple products/ service : Open up public procurement to 98% SMEs misalnya di kompleks perkantoran atau tiap perumahan ada hawker center yang bersih. Dan diprioritaskan buat orang-orang domisili lokal " "" "3. Access to finance (bukan sinterklas model atau penyertaan modal model lho!). Ini menjadi mekanisme "graduation facility" (yang lulus can be accompanied into mainstream business development support services). Program ini diperuntukkan kepala mereka yang kapasitasnya ada, memiliki growth ambitions for their enterprises) dan masih dapat berkembang (berarti screeningnya harus ketat dan tidak boleh ada sogok menyogok), lalu dipilih SME di industri apa (misalnya tourism kek yang diprioritaskan kalau ada, atau IoT kek dll). Tetap menggunakan prinsip 4C bank, ada collateral dll, tapi sangat ringan pengambaliannya. Sedapat mungkin tidak dalam cash, tapi dalam bentuk “specific barang/ bahan”. Caranya dengan sedikit-sedikit kasih kredit, lalu SME ini dinilai dari disipllin pengambaliannya. Memang ujung-ujungnya kalau gak bisa dibalikkan maka si pelaku akan tetap statusnya dan harus membayar seringan mungkin atau mentok-mentok di “waive”. Include special provisions such as quotas for local domicile." "" "4. Promote the development of business angel networks ataupun koperasi targeting investments in local domicile enterprises." "" "5. Zoning/ Site and premises : jadi disiapkan akses taman buat jualan seperti hawker-center yang sering dilewati orang, di tengah keramaian, dan bersih dan aman,Level RT/ RW/Kelurahan" "" "6. Training yang specific, bukan yang umum dan sekedarnya. Merevitalisasi peran “PLUT”, tapi trainernya selektif harus pebisnis juga, bukan karyawan. Ada retainer, ada insentif uang berdasarkan kesuksesan membimbing misalnya dihitung dari revenue mentee nya tapi uang komisinya dari government lah." "" "7. Buat large corporations yang terlibat gerakan ini diberi tax incentive program. " "" "8. Dibuat sekolah (TK-SD) untuk para anak-anak SMEs disekitar tempat berjualan.  Secara jangka panjang, eksposure anak-anak yang melihat proses berdagang ini (Walaupun bapaknya pebisnis mikro) akan menciptakan neuron pathways dan firing neuron pruning entrepeneurial mereka. Mereka sekolah entrepeneur gratis ketika melihat bapak-ibunya berdagang. " "" "Finally, tidak semua bisa naik “pangkat”, atau secara alami lepas dari SME 98% dan berkembang menjadi businessman dengan skala beda. Setiap orang memiliki kapasitas berbeda." "" "Membagi-bagi uang jelas bukan pilihan, malah akan membuka peluang poverty trap lebih kentara lagi, as per "Poverty Trap" theory by Esther Duflo. World Bank also do not condone this this santa-claus mode.
2021-06-12 Takeaway from Prof. Frank Cespedes' webinar on 23 April 2021 for Harvard Business School G...
Takeaway from Prof. Frank Cespedes' webinar on 23 April 2021 for Harvard Business School GMP Alumni "Selling After the Crisis: What is Changing and Why?" where the 60+ years sequential AIDA hierarchy of effects model that has been the basis for most sales pipeline, training and CRM models must be revisited, as buying journeys in most markets are now a dynamic process that is: explore, evaluate, engage in parallel streams via tech tools." "" "In Sales Tasks and Management Requirements there will be more emphasis on value-added of rep in customer interactions, more X-functional interactions in selling (as the term Dynamic Buying means). " "" "Multiple impacts in sales, due to wave of data revolution:" "- increasing scrutiny by finance and impact on sales careers" "- shift in productivity efforts to front-end of value chain: COGS has decreased but SG&A has increased as % of firms' costs." "- in people area (hiring, training, recruiting and evaluating the inherent challenges are getting harder as selling becomes a more data-intensive activity. Despite spending 20% more per-capita on sales training versus other functions, ROI is still disappointing. " "- in process area (sales models, relevant metrics, compensation/ incentives), many of them are based on obsolete assumptions. The sales models need rethinking to increase customer-contact and manage online/offline interactions in buying journeys." "- in partnering, the multi-channel go-to-market is a required norm, meaning : online and offline ARE not either/or choices. The implications are apparent for required skills, data, and training efforts." "- pricing : Value Pricing will be promoted if the people can make the most of data analytics. Yes there will be more tools available for price testing, but as in any corporations, the corporate immune will create high inertia. In addition, the relevant units of customer value are changing. " "- in productivity area: specially in a service economy domain, the sales productivity becomes a social issue as well as a driver of a company growth." "" "More can be learned from the book below.

It is what you can do that is important, not what others cannot do. With the one or two most obvious competitors, however, you may need to be very explicit: “Unlike Cisco’s firewall solution, our software can operate ….”" ">Use simple sentences, not multi-tiered compound sentences." ">Use analogs, as long as you are clarifying rather than hyping. You can say you are using the Google model for generating revenues, as long as you don’t say you expect to be the next Google." ">Finally, the sentence that introduces your company should sell your company, not just describe it. "" "Kenyan runner Abel Mutai was only a few meters from the finish line, but got confused with the signs and stopped, thinking he had finished the race. A Spanish man, Ivan Fernandez, was right behind him and, realizing what was going on, started shouting to the Kenyan to keep running. Mutai did not know Spanish and did not understand. Realizing what was going on, Fernandez pushed Mutai to victory. A reporter asked Ivan, "Why did you do this?" Ivan replied, "My dream is that one day we can have some sort of community life where we push ourselves and help each other win." The reporter insisted "But why did you let the Kenyan win?" Ivan replied, "I didn't let him win, he was going to win. The race was his." The reporter insisted and asked again, "But you could have won!" Ivan looked at him and replied: "But what would be the merit of my victory? What would be the honor of this medal? What would my Mother think of it?" The values are transmitted from generation to generation. What values do we teach our children”" "" "The above familiar story presents a virtue in humanity. "" "The concept is illustrated in the Venn diagram below. " "🍇 Imagine a team of three: the "hacker, hustler, hipster" trio is a term often used in the startup world. Such a team should have complementary skills and networks but a shared objective, embodying the diverse experts model. This is something we also see in Design Thinking. However, if we rely solely on uniqueness, the common ground, or area of intersection, is relatively small." "🍇 Then there's the homogeneous team model – a model not recommended for agile teams due to its lack of diversity." "🍇 Ideally, we should strive for a "heterogeneous PLUS inclusive team". This approach, represented by the 'Mickey Mouse shaped' Venn diagram, encompasses the largest area of common ground." "" "How can organizations foster such teams? They must establish a fearless, psychologically safe environment, encouraging team members to freely express their thoughts and feelings. Listening is crucial, but ensuring everyone, especially minorities, voice their ideas is even more vital. Remember: "Never kill an idea, no matter how outlandish it might seem."" 2019-12-31 A new year message that may help to count blessings in preparing the resolution : created ...
A new year message that may help to count blessings in preparing the resolution : created by Jean d’Ormesson (The Train of My Life) :" "" "At birth, we get on the train and meet our parents. And we believe they will always travel with us. Yet at a station, our parents will get off the train, leaving us alone to continue the journey. " "" "As time goes by, other people get on the train. And they will be important, our siblings, our friends, our children, even the love of our lives. Many will resign (even possibly the love of our lives), and leave a more or less great void" "Others will be so discreet that we won't realize they've left their seats This train journey will be full of joys, sorrows, expectations, hellos, goodbyes and farewells. " "" "Success is to have good relations with all passengers as long as we give our best" "" "We don't know which station we'll be down to, so live happily, love and forgive" "It is important to do so because when we get off the train, we will have to leave only beautiful memories to those who will continue their journey" "" "Let's be happy with what we have and thank heavens for this fantastic journey" "Also, thank you for being one of the passengers on my train" "" "And if I have to get down to the next station, I'm glad I've come a long way with you" "" "-Jean d'Ormesson

Passion : it is not a hyped word : neuroscience explains. It lends the story on how a person may or may not derive the traits of #entrepreneur. Thanks to Daniel Siegel. " "" "It dates back when you were a baby when your brain must be conditioned to be healthy to allow the overproduction of the neurons. It continues when "you were a child, developing in ways that are generalized learning everything you can about everything you can. Then when you reach an adolescence, this is when you begin to find your #PASSION, to actually find things you like, the things you really love doing, and to drive your development in that way. What happens in the brain during this period is the pruning of the neuron connections : it is a use it or a lose it principle underneath it that if you don't use, something you're gonna lose , so if you like sports, life music, dancing" or researching or trading, hence "do those things so you continue to establish those circuits". " "" ""Then there is this myelinization. This is the process that strengthening whatever "left" during the pruning process. It focuses your attention to be aware of your emotions, aware of other people to be engaging in activities, to be doing things with your thoughts, that actually reinforce the parts of your brain you want to hold on to".

A message came this morning about an euphoria of the authority that they will have more unicorns coming. I have posted about the calling for #startups to focus in maximizing values to founders, society, investors and customers. Sometimes it means maximum valuation ('unicorn'), but it isn't necessary always. I found the writing of Emma McGowan represents my thoughts." "" "“Being labeled a unicorn is like being labeled sexy by People Magazine. It might be true to some, but it’s based entirely on perspective,” .... “As we all know, valuation in the startup world is far more art than science, and likely to be influenced by trend, popularity or ‘irrational exuberance.’” So, valuation is pretty nebulous. And that $1 billion mark? It’s arbitrary. I mean, it looks nice, sure. But all it indicates is the fact that your company has raised a lot of money and investors believe in you. You don’t get magical powers when you hit that unicorn mark. Also, more and more unicorn startups are “worth” more than $1 billion, without actually making any money.” " "" "Another illustration is this : “Every star in the sky—including our own sun—will eventually run out of the fuel it burns to shine so bright. When it happens to a particularly massive star, the end is spectacular. At some point, as the fusion process begins to create heavier and heavier elements, the core of the star becomes too densely packed to survive. The star collapses in on itself, cannibalized by the overwhelming power of gravity. And then it explodes, ejecting a tsunami of matter and energy, creating a shockwave that threatens anything in its immediate vicinity” - Kevin Dowd on October 20, 2019 in https://lnkd.in/dBzXZDuu when he questions the future profitability of airbnb and such." "" "Prof. Mihir Desai of Harvard Business School taught that the nirvana (finance wise) is the "free cash flow". He wrote "it is the purest measure of cash and forms the basis of valuation".

Anticipating people’s emotional reactions during a change process are considered important from early days and grow starts becoming very obvious in the age bracket 36-45. " "" "Meanwhile, the remaining competences (e). Understanding business models and how they change, (f). Making a great first impression (g). Planning and delivering training program, while they are needed and must have during 20-27 age bracket, become less and less required along with the maturity." "" "It is worth noting that "Being aware of how your actions affect others" has always been the most noticeable throughout all age brackets (20-27, 26-35,36-45,46-55, 56-65, and 66+) and being the highest at bracket 66+." 2019-09-17 Yes, "Private equity returns are not all they seem", FT."
Yes, "Private equity returns are not all they seem", FT." "" "I remembered a journal written by Steve Kaplan and Antoinette Schoar of MIT Sloan School of Management, "Private Equity Performance: Returns, Persistence and Capital Flows", Journal of Finance 60 (August 2005)." "" "" .... average fund returns net of fees approximately equal the S&P 500 although there is a large degree of heterogeneity among fund returns. Returns persists strongly across funds raised by individual private equity partnerships. The returns also improve with partnership experience. Better performing funds are more likely to raise follow-on funds and raise larger funds than funds that perform poorly. This relationship is concave so that top performing funds do not grow proportionally as much as the average fund in the market. At the industry level, ...., market entry in the private equity industry is cyclical. Funds (and partnerships) started in boom times are less likely to raise follow-on funds, suggesting that those funds subsequently perform worse. Aggregate industry returns are lower following a boom, but most of this effect is driven by the poor performance of new entrants, while the returns of established funds are much less affected by these industry cycles...."

2019-08-27 Nuclear power will fill 8-12% gap in 2040 energy mix. However, to envision Thorium fuel b...
Nuclear power will fill 8-12% gap in 2040 energy mix. However, to envision Thorium fuel based nuclear power plant to be built in Indonesia, is very alarming." "" "Their ecosystem technology adoption cycle is not as an early adopter but perhaps a conservative or laggard. (“Crossing the chasm” )." "" "* Scientists don’t have as much experience with Th. The biggest problem with Thorium is lacking in operational experience with it. " "* Thorium fuel is a bit harder to prepare. Thorium dioxide melts at 550 degrees higher temperatures than traditional UO2, so very high temperatures are required to produce high-quality solid fuel. Also,Th is quite inert, making it difficult to chemically process." "* Irradiated Thorium May be more dangerously radioactive in the short term. The Th-U cycle invariably produces some U-232, which decays to Tl-208, which has a 2.6 MeV gamma ray decay mode. Bi-212 also causes problems. These gamma rays are very hard to shield, requiring more expensive spent fuel handling and/or reprocessing." "* Thorium doesn’t work as well as U-Pu in a fast reactor. While U-233 an excellent fuel in the thermal spectrum, it is between U-235 and Pu-239 in the fast spectrum. So for reactors that require excellent neutron economy (such as breed-and-burn concepts), Thorium is not ideal.

2019-07-01 Prof. Nelson Repenning of MIT Sloan School of Management taught the Work Dynamics Design c...
Prof. Nelson Repenning of MIT Sloan School of Management taught the Work Dynamics Design concept in one of the courses I took in MIT Sloan Executive Education when completing the #ACE program. Since then my production line efficiency has been improved dramatically. While a Physical Work is easy to track because it’s visible, usually repetitive, and easy to see, a Creative Work is invisible and more variable, so workflow is harder to monitor. Make the invisible work visible so it can be systemized. Urge the use of visual management techniques, which can be as simple as post-it notes on a work board — to give a physical face to intellectual work. Giving invisible work this physical manifestation makes it much easier to monitor the progress of work as it moves through the organization from idea to physical or intellectual product." 2018-02-17 O&G will play a major role in non-hydro-renewables ! Oil (in the energy mix) will be reduced dramati...
O&G will play a major role in non-hydro-renewables ! Oil (in the energy mix) will be reduced dramatically from 11% in 1990 to be only 1% in 2040. The O&G company will see such reduction as business disruption needed as usual. Their goal is to maintain shareholders value and not necessarily to glorify the oil for the sake of it (nothing to do with peak oil etc). It is most likely they will invest more in non-hydro-renewables (17% of the mix). Their shareholder would mandate them to grow organically through renewables ! " "" "Renewable energy grows aggressively from 1% in 1990 to 17% in 2040. That still cannot replace the coal which contributes the largest (31%) in 2040 despite the 6% decrease from 1990 and Natural Gas which actually grows from 15% in 1990 to 24% in 2040. " "" "As large corporations, O&G have abundant human and technology resources’ spare capacity that can be rededicated to renewable after oil diminished. They cannot be as agile and as sharp as startup but they can act like a VC or PE with Very competent GP to sustain the growth of the post startup. O&G company will be a good alternative (if not the best ) collaborator to contribute to the non-hydro renewable growth or to sustain further. Graph’s Source : “World Energy Outlook”, IEA,2014

2018-02-15 HUMANITY : CUSTOMER SERVICE : In the industry where a loss is common, Southwestern Airline (which i ...
HUMANITY : CUSTOMER SERVICE : In the industry where a loss is common, Southwestern Airline (which i have never flown before) showed an example of what a customer service should be. Can you imagine a plane turns around, only few minutes after taking- off, to offload a passenger (a “mom” names Peggy Uhle) whose 24 year old son was in a death or life situation due to head injury. Not only that, according to the story , the airline which has had no responsibility or whatsoever to the injury, extend the helps beyond any measures by flying the Mom to the city where her son was located -- without Peggy (the Mom and the passenger) spending a dime . Humanity is a a rare asset nowadays. To see such instance I want to cherish and rejoice our race ..... bravo Southwestern Airlines
